cases.title: Use the current DEVAI CLI
cases.goal: Select and run one of the 61 registered actions. This catalogue case lists the 41 general actions; the five journey cases that follow cover the remaining 20 (audit, backlog, release ceremony, round tracking, triage) in the order an operator uses them.
preconditions: DEVAI is installed in an adopter repository.
The caller satisfies the selected action authority and consent contract.
triggers: A developer needs to inspect, initialize, check, sense, execute, record, or verify work.

mainFlow.action: Use `catalog actions`: List registered DEVAI actions as JSON.
Use `check`: Run a canonical check suite or one named check with fail-closed aggregate output.
Use `doctor`: Composite repo health check. Posture: --self (full DEVAI checks), --adopter (subset that applies to adopter repos), --auto (default; sniff repo-root for DEVAI shape).
Use `evidence collect`: Collect governed evidence from one declared source into harness state.
Use `evidence record`: Record one governed evidence kind through the append-only evidence boundary.
Use `evidence redact`: Apply a redaction policy to a record, re-link downstream, and log a redaction event
Use `evidence render`: Render one evidence view from canonical records.
Use `evidence verify`: Verify a declared evidence scope, including optional read-only chain-head inspection.
Use `init apply architect`: Apply the Architect-owned initialization projection with explicit write consent.
Use `init apply harness`: Apply the canonical harness projection with explicit Architect-initiated write consent.
Use `init apply owner`: Apply the Owner-owned initialization projection with explicit write consent.
Use `init plan`: Build the exact segmented bootstrap plan without authorizing a mutation.
Use `init bind`: Bind selected installed DEVAI contracts into an adopter repository.
Use `release check`: Evaluate release eligibility without granting publication authority.
Use `release drift`: Inspect and record release-runtime drift under the release controller.
Use `release status`: Read release-control status without persisting evidence or state.
Use `release verify`: Verify post-deployment release state under the release controller.
Use `round assess`: Compute or render the active round assessment and governed triage views.
Use `round close`: Execute the authorized round-close transition; never infer release or publication.
Use `round gap create`: Create a governed round gap record through the harness boundary.
Use `round gap list`: List governed gaps for the active round.
Use `round gap resolve`: Resolve a governed round gap through the harness boundary.
Use `round gap show`: Show one governed round gap.
Use `round plan`: Create or render Architect-owned round planning material from canonical inputs.
Use `round run`: Advance selected ready tasks within one active round through their declared executors.
Use `round seal`: Seal Architect-owned round material without publishing it.
Use `round status`: Read one governed round in place and report its schema-valid canonical status.
Use `sense inventory`: Render one canonical repository inventory slice without persistence.
Use `sense migrate`: Execute the DB-writing migration sensor with explicit Engineer write consent.
Use `sense record`: Persist or rebuild declared sensor readings through the harness boundary.
Use `sense run`: Run one resolved sensor kind or preset; per-kind effect and authority are enforced before execution.
Use `task escalate`: Escalate one round-subordinate task through hidden plumbing.
Use `task finish`: Finish one round-subordinate task and release its declared resources.
Use `task pause`: Pause one round-subordinate task on a governed gap.
Use `task queue add`: Add one task to an active round queue through hidden plumbing.
Use `task queue complete`: Complete one active-round queue item through hidden plumbing.
Use `task queue list`: List active-round queue items through hidden plumbing.
Use `task queue next`: Select the next ready active-round queue item through hidden plumbing.
Use `task resume`: Resume one paused round-subordinate task after its governed gap resolves.
Use `task start`: Start one round-subordinate task and provision only its declared resources.
Use `task status`: Read task and managed-resource status for one active round.

postconditions: The selected action returns its declared result envelope or a fail-closed refusal.
acceptanceCriteria: Every action reference resolves exactly once in the current action registry.
Together with the journey cases in this file, the use cases reference exactly the current registered action population.

cases.title: Observe one exact commit as the Auditor
cases.goal: Compute a deterministic scorecard for one exact commit and, when evidence is wanted, record a non-promoting Auditor observation of it.
preconditions: The repository carries a bound harness and the full commit sha of the head to observe is known.
The session declares the auditor role; `audit observe` admits no other initiator.
triggers: A maintainer wants a reproducible assessment of one exact commit that neither promotes readiness nor authorizes a release.

mainFlow.action: Run `audit scorecard --at <full-sha> --repo-root . --format json`: compute the deterministic scorecard for that exact commit without persisting audit artifacts or evidence.
Read the scorecard cells. PASS is a measurement; review, unknown, fail, and N/A remain non-claims and none of them ratifies anything.

Run `audit observe --at <full-sha> --repo-root . --as-role auditor --write`: regenerate inventory, scorecard, assessment, and backlog for that exact commit as non-promoting Auditor evidence through the harness boundary.
Run `evidence verify` over the declared scope to confirm the recorded observation is intact before citing it.

alternateFlows.when: The observation belongs to a round whose governance tracking is enabled.

steps.action: Run `audit observe --at <full-sha> --round <round-id> --as-role auditor --write`: the observation is recorded as a `finding_emitted` tracking event, as an observation and never as a verdict. Without `--round` nothing is attributed; a round is never inferred.

exceptions.when: `--at` names an abbreviated sha or a commit that is not the exact commit under audit.
exceptions.handling: The action refuses fail-closed; no partial artifact is written.

exceptions.when: The session role is not auditor or `--write` is absent.
exceptions.handling: `audit observe` is refused before any effect; `audit scorecard` still runs read-only.

postconditions: Any recorded audit artifact is bound to the exact commit, is non-promoting, and grants no authority to merge, publish, or close a round.
acceptanceCriteria: `audit scorecard` returns byte-identical results for the same commit and inputs.
`audit observe` requires the auditor role plus explicit write consent and records only Auditor evidence.

cases.title: Work the repository backlog as the Engineer
cases.goal: Record, inspect, and resolve repository backlog items (finding, proposition, note, or flaky-test) without opening or altering a round gap.
preconditions: The backlog store under .devai/state/backlog/ sits behind the harness boundary.
The session declares one of the roles the registry admits for backlog writes: owner, architect, inspector, engineer, or auditor.
triggers: A finding, proposition, note, or flaky test surfaces during work and must be kept without a round gap or a network call.

mainFlow.action: Run `backlog list --repo-root .`: list open repository backlog items without network access.

Run `backlog add --kind <finding|proposition|note|flaky-test> --title <title> --body <body> --as-role engineer --write`: record one schema-validated item under .devai/state/backlog/ through the harness boundary.
Run `backlog show <item-id>`: read the recorded item back by id without network access.
Do the remediation under the authority of the task that owns it; the backlog item grants none.

Run `backlog resolve <item-id> --resolution <commit|pull-request|record|task|item reference> --as-role engineer --write`: mark the item resolved with its resolution reference. The command never pauses, resolves, or otherwise alters a round gap.

alternateFlows.when: The item belongs to a governed round.

steps.action: Run `backlog add ... --round <round-id>`: round attribution is opt-in at creation and is never inferred from the session, the branch, or the active round. With governance tracking enabled the item is projected as a `backlog_item_projected` event.
Run `backlog list --round <round-id>`: narrow the listing to items attributed to that round at creation.
Run `backlog resolve <item-id> --resolution <reference> --write`: attribution is read from the item, never inferred at resolution.

exceptions.when: The kind is not one of finding, proposition, note, or flaky-test, or the title or body is missing.
exceptions.handling: `backlog add` refuses with a structured error and writes nothing.

exceptions.when: `backlog resolve` names an unknown item id or an empty resolution reference.
exceptions.handling: The action refuses; the item and every round gap stay untouched.

postconditions: Every recorded item validates against backlog-item.schema.json and carries its own round attribution or none.
Round gaps are unchanged by any backlog action.
acceptanceCriteria: Add and resolve require a permitted role plus explicit write consent; list and show are read-only and make no network call.
No backlog action infers a round.

cases.title: Rehearse and promote one exact release candidate as the Owner
cases.goal: Take one exact candidate through the recorded release lifecycle, from plan receipt to publication, rehearsing each state before granting any remote effect.
preconditions: The candidate is one exact commit under the bound release lifecycle policy.
Each persisted state requires its predecessor as law/policy/release-lifecycle.json orders them: preflight_passed, certified, prepared, exported, evidence_published, publication_dispatched.
The Owner holds a separate one-time authorization for each remote-write step and passes `--publish` explicitly.
triggers: The Owner decides to promote a candidate that has passed governed checks and wants every transition recorded and verifiable.

mainFlow.action: Run `release plan` for the candidate: resolve the lifecycle plan from canonical inputs and emit a deterministic plan receipt. Nothing is persisted; the candidate is `planned`.
Run `release check`: evaluate release eligibility without granting publication authority.
Run `release preflight --as-role inspector --write`: record `preflight_passed` for the exact candidate against the bound valid plan receipt. It grants no packaging or publication authority.

Run `release certify --as-role inspector --write`: record the Inspector certification transition through the protected certification provider and its content-addressed evidence sink; the candidate is `certified`.

Run `release prepare --write`: compose the certified candidate release material in memory and expose it only through the injected trusted two-phase artifact sink under Architect authority; the candidate is `prepared`. No remote effect, no pathname destination, no npm or tool subprocess.
Run `release export --write`: export the prepared candidate through the append-only artifact-sink extension with one protected aggregate signer; the candidate is `exported`. No remote effect.

Run `release offline-verify`: verify the exported candidate and its evidence bundle without network access and emit the deterministic offline-verification receipt. It persists no state and grants no transition.

Run `release evidence-publish --publish --as-role owner --write`: publish the exported evidence bundle under an Owner-issued one-time authorization bound to the passing offline-verification receipt; the candidate is `evidence_published`. The product is not published.

Run `release publish --publish --as-role owner --write`: dispatch the product publication under a separate Owner-issued one-time authorization and record `publication_dispatched`. Published evidence never authorizes it.
Run `release resume`: report the exact recorded lifecycle head and the states verifiable from receipts; `published` is derived only from a verified signed publication receipt.
Run `release verify`: verify the post-deployment release state under the release controller.

alternateFlows.when: The Owner rehearses the ceremony before granting any authority.

steps.action: Run `release status --repo-root . --format json`: read release-control status without persisting evidence or state.
Run `release plan`: read the deterministic plan receipt the ceremony will bind to.
Run `release resume`: read the recorded head for the candidate; the observation advances, repairs, and revives nothing.

alternateFlows.when: The ceremony is interrupted after a persisted state.

steps.action: Run `release resume` to learn the exact recorded head, then continue from the next state; no state is re-recorded and no gap in the chain is repaired implicitly.

alternateFlows.when: Runtime drift is suspected after publication.

steps.action: Run `release drift`: inspect and record release-runtime drift under the release controller.

exceptions.when: A state is requested whose required predecessor is not recorded for the exact candidate.
exceptions.handling: The action refuses; the lifecycle head is unchanged.

exceptions.when: `release evidence-publish` or `release publish` is invoked without `--publish` or without its own Owner one-time authorization.
exceptions.handling: The remote effect is refused before dispatch.

exceptions.when: `release offline-verify` fails or its receipt does not bind the exported artifacts byte for byte.
exceptions.handling: `release evidence-publish` refuses; nothing leaves the repository.

postconditions: Every persisted state is an appendable record bound to the exact candidate, and each remote effect was separately authorized by the Owner.
acceptanceCriteria: Read-only leaves (plan, check, status, offline-verify, resume) persist nothing and grant no transition.
The remote-write leaves require the owner role, explicit write consent, and `--publish`.

cases.title: Track one governed round in a GitHub issue
cases.goal: Opt one round into governance tracking, project its public-safe events into one GitHub issue, watch projection health, and switch tracking off without losing what was published.
preconditions: The round exists under law/policy/round-execution.json.
An authenticated `gh` boundary is available; DEVAI stores no token.
Tracking is disabled by default and remains so until the Owner activates it for exactly one round.
triggers: The Owner wants a public-safe projection of one round's governed findings and mediated actions.

mainFlow.action: Run `init bind --tracking-adapter github-issues --tracking-repository <owner/name> --as-role architect --write` (dry run by default): bind the repository capability, materializing the tracking config, the reconciliation workflow, and the project binding.

Run `round tracking enable --round <round-id> --publish --as-role owner --write`: record the Owner authorization that activates tracking and bounded public projection for exactly that round. `--publish` is never inferred from the binding.
Run `round tracking status --round <round-id>`: report canonical event counts and remote projection health as independent axes, with no network call.

Run `round tracking sync --round <round-id> --publish --as-role owner --write`: reconcile the round's sealed projection outbox against the remote issue idempotently; a missing issue is never recreated implicitly.
Run `round tracking disable --round <round-id> --pending freeze --as-role owner --write`: disable tracking for the round, freezing pending events and never deleting an already published projection.

alternateFlows.when: The projection lags or the remote is unreachable.

steps.action: Run `round tracking status --round <round-id>`: the projection reads pending, failed, or unreachable while round readiness stays a separate axis; a remote failure never manufactures or withdraws a verdict.
Run `round tracking sync --round <round-id> --publish --as-role owner --write` again once the remote is reachable; the reconciliation is idempotent.

exceptions.when: `round tracking enable` or `round tracking sync` is invoked without `--publish`.
exceptions.handling: The remote-write is refused; publication consent is never inferred.

exceptions.when: The bound tracking repository does not match the remote, or a supplied authority session fails validation.
exceptions.handling: The action refuses rather than re-targeting or silently downgrading the chain identity.

postconditions: Only DEVAI-mediated actions are tracked, every projected event is public-safe, and a disabled round keeps its published projection.
acceptanceCriteria: Enable, sync, and disable require the owner role, explicit write consent, and `--publish`; status is read-only and offline.
A repository without a tracking binding behaves exactly as before the feature existed.

cases.title: Classify a sensor failure before remediation
cases.goal: Turn one failing or reviewing SensorReading into a recorded, deterministic classification and remediation route before anything is changed.
preconditions: One schema-valid SensorReading is available as a file.
The session declares a role the registry admits for `triage classify`: owner, architect, inspector, engineer, or auditor.
triggers: A sensor reports fail or review and the route to remediation must be chosen before any product code, sensor, or policy is touched.

mainFlow.action: Run `sense run <kind> --repo-root . --format json` and keep the reading: one SensorReading is the only input triage accepts.

Run `triage classify --input <reading.json> --as-role inspector --write`: deterministically classify the reading as plant_bug, sensor_error, policy_issue, reference_gap, or inconclusive, and record its route (discipline and action) through the harness boundary.
Follow the recorded route under its own authority and cost; the classification is neither proof that remediation succeeded nor permission to mutate product code.
Run `sense run <kind>` for a fresh observation and `check` for governed validation once the route is worked.

steps.action: `triage classify` records the `escalate_to_human` route; the uncertainty is explicit and never becomes a positive claim.

alternateFlows.when: The classification is reference_gap and the route is `emit_rgr`.

steps.action: Run `round gap create` for the active round: the reference gap becomes a governed round gap record through the harness boundary.

alternateFlows.when: The reading belongs to a round whose governance tracking is enabled.

steps.action: Run `triage classify --input <reading.json> --round <round-id> --as-role inspector --write`: the classification is recorded as a `finding_classified` tracking event. Without `--round` nothing is attributed; a round is never inferred.

exceptions.when: `--input` is missing, unreadable, or not a schema-valid SensorReading.
exceptions.handling: The action refuses fail-closed and records no route.

exceptions.when: The session role is not admitted or `--write` is absent.
exceptions.handling: The harness-write is refused before any classification is persisted.

postconditions: One classification and route are recorded for the reading; the reading itself and the sensed surface are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: The same reading classifies identically on every run.
An inconclusive reading always routes to a human.

cases.title: Activate experimental agent dispatch for a bounded period
cases.goal: Let the Owner permit experimental, non-promoting agent dispatch in one repository for a bounded period, with named runtimes, models, disciplines and budgets inside the experimental-execution policy ceilings.
preconditions: law/policy/experimental-execution.json is the framework policy (ADR-MDL-0005, ADR-MDL-0006).
Experimental dispatch is off until the Owner activates it, and the activation expires.
triggers: The Owner wants agents to attempt engineer or inspector tasks under experimental policy.

mainFlow.action: Run `round dispatch activate --input <activation.json> --as-role owner --write --experimental`: validate the Owner-authored activation against its schema, expiry window, and every policy ceiling, then record it in .devai/state/experimental/activation.json.

Run `round dispatch --round <round-id> --as-role architect --write --experimental`: dispatch the round's admitted agent tasks through the experimental ladder in per-attempt worktrees; a contained, completed attempt awaits human review and an exhausted ladder ends experimental_blocked.

exceptions.when: Any role other than the Owner, or a missing --write or --experimental, invokes the activation.
exceptions.handling: The action is refused before any byte is written; experimental consent is never implied by --write.

exceptions.when: The activation is schema-invalid, expired, valid for more than the policy's maximum days, or wider than a ceiling.
exceptions.handling: The action refuses with the specific code and leaves any earlier activation untouched.

exceptions.when: A dispatched attempt writes outside its discipline's Article 6 paths, or a journal attempt is uncertain after a crash.
exceptions.handling: The attempt fails with EXPERIMENTAL_WRITE_SCOPE_VIOLATION; uncertain work blocks the round with TASK_DISPATCH_UNCERTAIN until a human runs task escalate.

postconditions: Exactly one validated, expiring activation is in force, and only runtime state holds it.
acceptanceCriteria: Activation requires the owner role, --write, and --experimental.
No action writes an experimental activation under .devai/config, and no file there is read as one.

cases.title: Run a campaign round through the governed runtime
cases.goal: Project a campaign plan onto runtime state, materialize an open round's tasks through the single queue, and record the human ratification of reviewed work separately from merge.
preconditions: The campaign plan validates against law/schemas/campaign.schema.json.
The round is open in the plan and has an active governed round authorization.
triggers: The Architect opens a campaign round and wants its tasks in the runtime.

mainFlow.action: Run `campaign status --campaign <CMP-id>`: read the plan beside runtime task state and every named drift, writing nothing.
Run `campaign materialize --campaign <CMP-id> --round <round-id> --as-role architect --write`: write the round's tasks through the round task queue exactly as campaign-execution.json maps them.
Run `round ratify --round <round-id> --task <task-id> --decision accept --as-role owner --write` once a reviewed task awaits human review: it moves to pre_merge; merging stays a separate human act.

exceptions.when: A task record already exists with a different request.
exceptions.handling: campaign materialize refuses with TASK_RECORD_CONFLICT before writing anything.

exceptions.when: round ratify targets a task that is not awaiting human review, or is invoked by a role other than the Owner or Architect.
exceptions.handling: The ratification is refused and nothing is recorded.

postconditions: Plan and runtime agree or their drift is named; every ratification is a recorded human decision separate from merge.
acceptanceCriteria: campaign materialize writes only through the round task queue.
round ratify never merges, pushes, or closes a round.

cases.title: Upgrade an adopter repository to the installed DEVAI version
cases.goal: Let the Architect move an adopter from its bound devai_version to the installed package version in one governed operation that names every adopter-facing change first and refuses anything that needs a decision.
preconditions: The repository is bound: .devai/config/project.json carries devai_version and .devai/config/authority-policy.json exists.
The newer @aarusso-nyx/devai is installed and law/policy/adopter-migrations.json ships in it.
triggers: The adopter bumps the pinned DEVAI package version.

mainFlow.action: Run `init upgrade --target . --as-role architect`: plan the move from the manifest entries in range, listing the files that would change, the owned keys a rebind would retire, the declarations that replace a changed default, the stale version stamps and the new obligations, without writing.

Run `init upgrade --target . --as-role architect --write`: run the bind segments in canonical order through the bind journal, require policy-materialization-current, authority-enforcement and constitution-binding to pass, and record .devai/config/upgrade-receipt.json.

exceptions.when: Rebinding the adopter policy would retire an owned project.json key the source does not declare, such as ci_economy.attested_rc.
exceptions.handling: The upgrade refuses with INIT_UPGRADE_RETIREMENT_UNDECLARED, naming the key, before any byte is written.

exceptions.when: A doctor post-check fails after the segments ran.
exceptions.handling: The upgrade restores every byte it wrote and refuses with INIT_UPGRADE_POSTCHECK_FAILED, naming the failing checks.

postconditions: devai_version equals the installed version and the upgrade receipt records the move.
acceptanceCriteria: A second run at the same version writes nothing.
No owned key is retired by an upgrade.
